prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Scope: authorized, traceable hospital dispensing/returns. Aliases: Cinderwake=Pharmacy Fulfillment Robot; Juniper=Pharmacy Verification Station; Tallowmere=Medication Return Kiosk; Larkspur=Registered Nurse; Morrowglass=Medication Order Gateway; Bluejay=Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler; Copperfield=Pharmacy Technician; Stonewake=Biomedical Engineer. Producers: Morrowglass—Order Reconciliation Snapshot; Clinical Pharmacist—Dose Exception Review Slip; Copperfield—Cold Chain Handoff Card; Cinderwake—Priority Refill Tote Tag; Juniper—Batch Release Note; Hospital Courier—Pneumatic Capsule Seal Record; East Tube Dispatch Console—Tube Route Exception Ticket; Charge Nurse—Cabinet Downtime Notice; Medication Safety Officer—Diversion Review Packet; Tallowmere—Return Bin. Morrowglass validates patient/product/dose/route/timing; holds unresolved/canceled/duplicate/superseded orders; rejects inconsistent/incomplete updates with reasons. Release requires order/instruction/product/destination agreement and identifiers/time/credentials. Cinderwake consumes Snapshot, reconciles active orders/dispenses/cabinet balances by stable order identifier; retains clinical context, timestamps/transaction identifiers; verifies current authorization, excludes cancellations, replaces superseded values, flags duplicates, conservatively subtracts partial dispenses. Patient/medication/quantity disagreement holds transaction; audit records matches/differences/disposition. Copperfield requires discrepancy-free reconciliation before routine replenishment; verifies contents/packaging/lot/expiry/cold-chain, reverifies delays; never decides doses. Juniper blocks order/product/strength/quantity discrepancies; exceptions preserve evidence and require authorized disposition. Clinical Pharmacist assesses clinical concerns; inconclusive review stays held pending higher-level decision; corrections require authorized orders. Larkspur locks transactions, confirms nonadministration, never bypasses/substitutes. Observers immediately escalate serious/time-critical exceptions. Medication Safety Officer reviews diversion/high-risk/patient-harm events; IT Operations Specialist receives Packet, checks access/transaction/device logs without clinical changes, records software/connectivity findings. Stonewake evaluates mechanical/sensor faults and safe restoration. Final disposition records reviewer/evidence/released-corrected-withheld. Bluejay logs temperature/excursions/connectivity-loss; affected stock held refrigerated pending assessment. Courier records custody, collects closed ready-recorded bins. Reconcile manifests before Pneumatic Tube Network admission; East checks routes; West Tube Dispatch Console authorizes routing. Faults require holds/documented resolution/authorized

New part:
S161: North Ward Cabinet Controller applies the North Ward medication access rules when evaluating a cabinet transaction.
S162: Its ward-specific configuration defines permitted medication locations, access roles, and transaction limits for each cabinet.
S163: The configuration associates each medication location with the product identifiers and quantity thresholds used by the ward.
S164: Cabinet availability is calculated from the last confirmed inventory count and subsequent recorded movements.
S165: Configured maximum and minimum quantities guide replenishment decisions without overriding an active clinical restriction.
S166: Access rules require an authenticated user role appropriate to the requested medication and transaction type.
S167: High-risk medication locations can require an additional confirmation before a removal is accepted.
S168: The controller rejects a transaction when its location mapping does not match the reconciled medication identity.
S169: Configuration changes are versioned, reviewed, and recorded with the effective time and approving authority.
S170: If the controller has not received a current approved configuration, it prevents routine dispensing and reports the condition for investigation.
S171: Bluejay maintains a time-stamped temperature history for each refrigerated medication compartment and raises an alarm when a configured limit is exceeded.
S172: Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler applies approved upper and lower temperature limits to each monitored compartment.
S173: Calibrated probes report readings at configured intervals, and the cooler records probe identity and calibration status with each reading.
S174: Refrigerated stock is identified by medication, lot, and expiration date so that each unit remains traceable to its storage history.
S175: When readings exceed a limit or a probe becomes unavailable, the affected stock is marked ineligible for routine dispensing.
S176: The cooler preserves the affected stock in its current controlled environment while the condition is assessed.
S177: Sensor-monitored Medication Cooler uses the handoff card to compare a transfer’s recorded custody time with its temperature history.
S178: A Clinical Pharmacist reviews excursion details and determines whether affected stock may be released, quarantined, or discarded under pharmacy policy.
S179: The cooler retains the disposition status against the affected lot and prevents stock marked ineligible from being selected for routine dispensing.
S180: Authorized access to refrigerated compartments is recorded with the user identity, access time, and affected stock identifiers.
S181: Door-open duration is monitored so that an access event that threatens temperature control can be distinguished from a brief inspection.
S182: Temperature alarms remain active during loss of network connectivity, and local records are retained until communication is restored.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
